newsitem.title: USA: Second NASD examiner may sue association - lawyer.
newsitem.headline: Second NASD examiner may sue association - lawyer.

text.p: A second National Association of Securities Dealers examiner may file a lawsuit within days charging that NASD officials improperly discouraged him from probing possible securities violations at major firms, a lawyer for Theresa Carr said.

Carr, a former senior compliance examiner in NASD's district 10 office in New York City, filed a $20 million damage suit in New York State Supreme Court Sept 4 against the association and William O'Connell, the district's assistant director for fixed income.
She charged that NASD "maliciously" discharged her for aggressively probing "pay-to-play" in the municipal market.

Now a second examiner in NASD's district 10 office wants to sue NASD for interfering with probes of major firms, Carr lawyer Jacob Zamansky, a partner with Singer Zamansky in New York City, said in a telephone interview.

"Another examiner -- I can't give out his name -- has visited with me and is contemplating a similar lawsuit," Zamansky said. "I'm in the process of evaluating his case. He knows Tess Carr. He's confirmed a lot of what she said."
Zamansky added, "This examiner was told not to investigate certain things involving some of the same major firms. Basically he was shut up and told not to proceed."
Zamansky said the second examiner's charges do not involve municipal bond probes. "It's not muni bonds. It's a different area with the same thing -- Don't step on the big industry toes."
The second examiner, like Carr, also alleges that key internal files on investigations mysteriously disappeared, Zamansky said.
Zamansky said he agreed to a request by NASD lawyers for an additional 30 days, until Nov 5, to file a response to Carr's lawsuit.
NASD's lawyer, Joseph Warin, a partner with Gibson Dunn & Crutcher in Washington, was unavailable for comment.
